FAQ

Eurovision Games — frequently asked questions

Quick answers to the questions hosts and players ask most. The three most-asked — creating, joining, and leaving — are highlighted at the top. The rest are in an accordion below. For deeper detail see the rule book, scoring formulas, and setup guide.

Creating a room

Sign in (email-only — we send a one-tap magic link), click "Create Room", pick the round count (1-3 quiz rounds) and max players (2-20). A 6-character room code and shareable link appear instantly. The host owns the room until they leave or delete it.

Defaults that work

  • 3 quiz rounds — enough warm-up without dragging.
  • Max 20 players — the upper limit; smaller rooms feel snappier.
  • A default per-pair duel cap of 3 (rematches counted) — prevents one-target grinding.

Joining a room

Use the join link the host shared (one tap, no account), or open Eurovision Games, click "Join Room", and type the 6-character code plus your display name. Late joiners can still play duels and quiz, but predictions lock once the host advances the phase.

  • Easiest path: tap the join link the host shared. One step, no account.
  • Manual: open Eurovision Games → Join Room → enter the 6-character code plus a display name.
  • Late joiners can still play trivia and duels, but predictions are locked once the host advances past Predictions.

Leaving or deleting a room

Tap your name in the room header → "Leave room". Your slot frees up; your scored points stay frozen on the leaderboard so the rest of the room is unaffected. Hosts have an extra "Delete room" option in the host panel that ends the session for everyone — a 5-second confirmation prevents accidents.

  • Players tap their name in the room header → Leave room. Banked points stay frozen on the leaderboard.
  • Hosts have an extra Delete room option in the host panel — a 5-second confirmation prevents accidents.
  • Accidental leave? Re-join with the same code and display name. Your points are restored.

More questions

Couldn’t find an answer?

Hop into a room and ask the host — or check the About page for direct contact details.
